findings.body:
**Stale branch — merging this will fight current `main` and can erase the v2 skill router.**

This PR is based on the v1.6.2 dogfood commit (~41 commits behind `main`). `main` already has the Local & CI Companion reframe **and** a fifth capability ([`apply-review`](apply-review/SKILL.md)), frontmatter `version: "2.5.1"`, and apply-review activation triggers. This description still advertises only **four** capabilities and omits apply-review routing phrases ("what did the CI review say", "apply the AI review's fixes").

`git merge-tree` reports `SKILL.md` **changed in both**. If the conflict is resolved toward this branch, consumers lose the apply-review entry point while `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/apply-review/` still ships on `main`.

**Fix:** close this PR, or rebase onto current `main` and re-diff — expected result is empty / no remaining narrative work.

**Outdated pin and overstated parity relative to the merge target.**

Current `main` documents pinning `@v2.1.0` (moving major `@v2`; skill package `version: "2.5.1"`) and carefully says local and CI share methodology/severity model while **Iteration-Aware Review may dedupe on CI round 2+** — local stays a full pass. This line reintroduces `@v1.4.2` and claims **"identical reviews"**, which steers Marketplace/skills.sh readers onto an old major and sets a false expectation when CI shortens follow-up rounds.

```suggestion
`@v2.1.0` on both surfaces guarantees the same methodology and severity
model (CI may additionally dedupe on round 2+ via Iteration-Aware
Review; local reviews stay a full pass).
```

Only apply after rebasing onto `main` (where the surrounding IAR paragraph still exists).

**Install guidance freezes readers on the v1 line.**

Comment says "Latest v1.x" and the reproducible pin is `@v1.4.2`; the note two paragraphs down still says published tags "v1.0.0–v1.4.2". Current release line is **v2.x** (tags through `v2.5.1`). After a stale-branch merge this becomes the copy-paste install consumers follow from the parent skill.

On current `main` this block already reads "Latest v2.x" / `npx skills add DailybotHQ/ai-diff-reviewer@v2.1.0` with a tag note covering `@v2`. Drop this branch tip rather than editing in isolation.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this branch is ~2 months and **41 commits behind `main`**, and `main` already ships the Local & CI Companion framing this PR set out to introduce. A merge would conflict on `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` and, if resolved toward this branch, would **regress** the published skill router from the current v2.5.1 / five-capability docs back to a v1.6.2-era four-capability snapshot.

## Findings table

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:3` | Stale branch: frontmatter still routes **four** capabilities; `main` has five (`apply-review`) at `version: "2.5.1"` |
| 2 | 🚨 critical | `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:51` | Pin example `@v1.4.2` + "identical reviews" — current line is `@v2` / `v2.5.1`, and CI parity is methodology-level (IAR may shorten round 2+) |
| 3 | ⚠️ warning  | `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:98` | Install snippet still says "Latest v1.x" and pins `@v1.4.2`; tag note stops at v1.4.2 |

## Context (cross-cutting)

- **Merge-base** is `7f75f05` (`chore(release): dogfood vendored ai-diff-reviewer to v1.6.2`, 2026-07-15). **`main` HEAD** is v2.5.1 skill sync (2026-09-23).
- `git merge-tree` reports **`skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` changed in both**.
- On `main`, the H1 is already `# AI Diff Reviewer — Local & CI Companion Skill`, with the Two-audiences frame, Surface column, flows-before-install order, and Default-flow header — plus later work this branch never saw: **`apply-review`**, IAR / skip-review-label **CI-only surfaces**, `@v2.1.0` / `@v2` pins, and Grok CLI / Pi / OpenCode in the agent list.
- Two-dot `git diff main HEAD -- skills/` would also drop `apply-review/SKILL.md` and regress sibling skill docs if the branch tip were taken wholesale; the PR's own commits only touch this one file, but a conflict resolution that keeps "theirs" is the failure mode to avoid.
